experience.designTarget: Preserve the blue workstation and primary left rail. Saved cards distinguish scenes and reusable objects with labeled pose schematics, metadata and explicit copy actions. An isolated definition frames its object; returning to a scene restores useful room framing. The Simulation dock shares the timeline clock, shows available interactions, matching behavior delays, evaluated object states and real renderer visibility. Reset restores initial scene state; no-match feedback explains how to author an effect. Engineering mode adds identities and coordinates. Ordinary Save/history remain canonical. The refined blue workstation keeps its established panel layout. Scene Graph rows contain assets only, with one selected-object icon toolbar. Context menus expose existing object/viewport/preset/saved-scene commands, support keyboard entry and focus restoration, and honor preview, locking, busy and proposal constraints. Inspector identity precedes environment tools; detailed navigation guidance is disclosed on demand. Opacity uses the existing property selector and numeric keyframe fields, labeled zero-to-one material factors. Play/scrub visibly fades the same mesh and its directional shadow, zero opacity identifies a transparent object with Reveal in editor recovery, and Editor restores original translucency without editing saved content. Native companion capability negotiation explicitly falls back with a fading-specific explanation when unsupported. Timeline clips and pose markers occupy separate pointer rows. The settings pane stays beside tracks and identifies the selected pose. Cinematic is the third continuous interpolation choice, with exact endpoints, smooth easing, bounded per-take arcs and asset-aware sway; Step remains an explicit instantaneous option. Reduced motion removes decorative arcs and sway. A Scene Graph title click enters inline rename. Edit room features opens and focuses actual controls after React commits room geometry. Photo authoring accepts one or two views, estimates scale automatically and exposes optional relative scaling. Scene Timeline has one continuous current-time line and a connected wide grabber. Captured-pointer scrubbing previews canonical scene state live, pauses playback, leaves authored tracks unchanged, supports keyboard seeking and exposes current-time recovery outside a zoomed window. The page title and Parallax icon occupy the upper left; the active scene has a distinct centered identity. Library has Assets and Environments tabs. Every saved edited/reconstructed room has an environment entry with rename, edit, apply and discovery deletion that retains scene copies. Environment editing uses the same live gizmos and synchronized Inspector selection. With a fixed asset selected, clicking a visible room surface places and aligns it at the clicked point without requiring overlays. Open doorframes and explicit appliance shapes distinguish physical features instead of showing every appliance as a cabinet. Scene Graph adds Assets and Groupings tabs and one Group toolbar icon. Modifier clicks, Shift ranges, Ctrl/Command A, modifier Space, arrow focus and Ctrl/Command G offer keyboard selection and grouping. No/marginal selection opens a named member chooser; a multiple selection groups immediately and can be renamed. Groups select and highlight together in the scene, expose member inspection and right-click commands, and use the same Move/Rotate/Scale tools with a clear numeric group Inspector. Room members rotate upright and scale uniformly. Live preview commits once at release; Escape/pointer cancellation restores the saved poses. Lock and automatic-placement limits remain visible. Membership changes and ungrouping retain entities, room features and hierarchy. Assistant group edits use the same canonical preview/review/Apply and safe input preflight. Exclusion zones appear as lightly filled outlined boxes only during environment editing. The Room Inspector has a compact exclusion section for discovering blockers and adding manual reservations. Automatic envelopes follow their modeled blocker on a named support face. Editing an envelope detaches it, and deleting it stays deleted without suppressing real solid obstacles. Exclusion volumes never become observed furniture or placement surfaces. Finish environment editing clears room selection and removes the volumes from normal scene rendering. Library Environments adds a single plus entry point opening a rounded, focus-restoring setup dialog: independent saved-room/preset copy, empty editable shell, or one/two-photo reconstruction. Photo setup shows private local thumbnails, explicit consent, real import/inference progress with reduced-motion support, cancel/retry, an actual orbitable room proposal with expandable review notes, and Apply into an independently saved editable environment. Preserved source rooms, reload continuity and configured-provider refusal remain observable. Unpaid development inference proves the UI workflow only; live layout accuracy, configured production readiness and phone AR are separate gates. Individual grouped assets retain regular controls; Groups explicitly selects whole groups. Scene Graph order follows drag live and saves one Undo step. Group floor clicks preserve spacing atomically. The continuous floor distinguishes usable furniture clearance from low blocked gaps. One Assistant frame contains header controls, animated pending work and retained clarification exchanges, with concise first-person review and immediate removal of stale actions. Working drafts persist without saved Library membership. Independent environment documents never create unnecessary Scene cards. A unified typed Library separates saved/working/legacy/archive views and supports collections, favorites, versions and pinned reuse. Named copies are idempotent, historical copies retain version-specific intent, and recovery preserves the original CAS revision. Environment keyboard history is scoped independently from its originating Scene; its tall canvas retains every transform control. Light/dark and narrow layouts remain readable.
